meta.name: Barbarossa
meta.note: Approximate reconstruction, and the coarsest in this project: a 1,600 km front reconstructed from nine dated lines. The theater is cut off at 45E, so it shows the ground that changed hands, not the whole Soviet Union. Ends at the high-water mark on 5 December, the day before the counteroffensive.

keyframes.label: Barbarossa. Three million men attack on a front of 1,600 km, the largest invasion in history.
Minsk is encircled. Three hundred thousand men are taken in the first pocket.
The Baltic states are overrun and the Dnieper is reached. Stalin, silent for eleven days, calls it a patriotic war.
The Smolensk pocket is cleared. Another 300,000 prisoners, and the road to Moscow is open.
Leningrad is cut off. The siege that follows lasts 872 days and kills perhaps a million civilians.
The pincers meet at Lokhvitsa, east of Kiev. Four Soviet armies are inside the ring.
Kiev. The largest encirclement ever achieved: around 600,000 men. Hitler turned south to do it, and spent the good weather doing it.
Vyazma and Bryansk. Moscow is declared under a state of siege; the government leaves for Kuibyshev. Stalin stays.
Rostov is taken. It is retaken by the Soviets nine days later — the first German retreat of the war.
The high-water mark. Reconnaissance troops see Moscow through binoculars in -30 degrees. The next morning the Soviet counteroffensive begins.
